hints: Focus on what lower pH really means for the same concentration, think about concentration of hydrogen ions in solution.
Statement 1 is about degree of dissociation, check if more dissociation would give more $\text{H}^+$ and a lower pH.
Look carefully at which H in $\text{HCO}_2\text{H}$ is actually acidic, and decide if statement 3 matches the pH evidence.
walkthrough:
**Link pH to hydrogen ion concentration**

Lower pH means higher $\text{H}^+$ concentration. Both acids start at the same concentration, so the one with lower pH must be releasing more $\text{H}^+$ into solution.

$$\text{pH} = -\log[\text{H}^+]$$

**Check statement 1**

Statement 1 says $\text{HCO}_2\text{H}$ dissociates more fully than $\text{HCN}$. More dissociation means more $\text{H}^+$ released per mole of acid. This directly explains the lower pH, so statement 1 is correct.

$$\text{HCO}_2\text{H} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+ + \text{HCO}_2^-$$

**Check statement 2**

It is true that $\text{HCO}_2\text{H}$ has two H atoms in its formula, but only one is acidic. The O-H hydrogen can be lost as $\text{H}^+$, the C-H hydrogen cannot. So counting total H atoms does not explain acidity.

$$\text{H-C(=O)-O-H: only the O-H is acidic}$$

**Check statement 3 and conclude**

A lower pH at the same concentration means a stronger acid, not a weaker one. Methanoic acid must be stronger than hydrocyanic acid, so statement 3 is the wrong way round. Only statement 1 explains the observation.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean all three statements explain the lower pH. Statement 2 does not explain it because only one H in methanoic acid is acidic, and statement 3 is factually wrong.
options.B: Incorrect. This would include statement 2 as an explanation. Students choose this by thinking more H atoms in the formula means more $\text{H}^+$ released, forgetting that the C-H hydrogen in $\text{HCO}_2\text{H}$ is not acidic.
options.C: Incorrect. This would include statements 2 and 3. Statement 3 claims methanoic acid is weaker, which is opposite to the evidence, since the stronger acid gives the lower pH.
options.D: Correct. Only statement 1 is a valid explanation. Greater dissociation of $\text{HCO}_2\text{H}$ gives a higher $[\text{H}^+]$ and therefore a lower pH than $\text{HCN}$ at the same concentration.
